items.stem: The Compromise of 1877 settled the disputed presidential election by —
items.stemEs: El Compromiso de 1877 resolvió la elección presidencial en disputa al —

choices.text: Readmitting the last former Confederate states to the Union after military rule
choices.textEs: Readmitir en la Unión a los últimos antiguos estados confederados tras el gobierno militar
choices.explanation: Readmission was already finished: Georgia, the last state, returned in July 1870. This is a real step of Reconstruction, seven years too early to be what 1877 settled.
choices.misconception: places the readmission of the Confederate states in 1877 rather than 1868-1870

choices.text: Withdrawing federal support from the last Republican state governments
choices.textEs: Retirar el apoyo federal a los últimos gobiernos estatales republicanos

choices.text: Awarding the disputed electoral votes to Samuel J. Tilden of New York
choices.textEs: Otorgar los votos electorales en disputa a Samuel J. Tilden de Nueva York
choices.explanation: The disputed votes went to Rutherford B. Hayes, and conceding them is what the Democrats traded for the withdrawal of federal support. Tilden held the larger popular vote and still lost the electoral count.
choices.misconception: reverses the outcome of the electoral dispute, handing the contested votes to the candidate who lost them

choices.text: Confirming that Samuel J. Tilden had won the national popular vote
choices.textEs: Confirmar que Samuel J. Tilden había ganado el voto popular nacional
choices.explanation: Tilden did win the popular vote, so this is true — and it is not what the Compromise did. The quarrel was over the electoral count in three states, and the Compromise settled who would take office.
choices.misconception: answers with a true fact about the election rather than with what the Compromise settled

items.dokRationale: The student retrieves what the Compromise did. Nothing has to be reasoned out from one fact to another, so recognising the withdrawal of federal support is recall rather than explanation.
items.explanation: The deadlock broke when Democrats let Hayes take office and Republicans ended the federal military backing that had kept their state governments standing in South Carolina, Louisiana and Florida. Those governments fell within months, which is why 1877 marks the end of Reconstruction.
items.explanationEs: El estancamiento se rompió cuando los demócratas permitieron que Hayes asumiera el cargo y los republicanos pusieron fin al respaldo militar federal que había sostenido a sus gobiernos estatales en Carolina del Sur, Luisiana y Florida. Esos gobiernos cayeron en pocos meses, por lo que 1877 marca el fin de la Reconstrucción.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable

items.stem: Why did the founding of the Ku Klux Klan in 1866 make it harder for Reconstruction governments to stay in power?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué la fundación del Ku Klux Klan en 1866 dificultó que los gobiernos de la Reconstrucción se mantuvieran en el poder?

choices.text: Southern Democrats regained control of the state legislatures by winning elections
choices.textEs: Los demócratas del Sur recuperaron el control de las legislaturas estatales ganando elecciones
choices.explanation: Democrats did take the legislatures back, and that is how Redemption was completed. It answers how power changed hands rather than what the Klan's founding did to make that possible.
choices.misconception: answers how Democrats regained power rather than how Klan violence made it possible

choices.text: Southern states disqualified Black voters with poll taxes and literacy tests
choices.textEs: Los estados del Sur descalificaron a los votantes negros con impuestos electorales y pruebas de alfabetización
choices.explanation: Those devices came two decades later, out of the constitutional conventions of the 1890s. In the Klan's first years disfranchisement was not yet written into law; it was enforced by violence.
choices.misconception: places legal disfranchisement in the 1860s rather than the 1890s

choices.text: Violence and intimidation kept Black voters and their allies from the polls
choices.textEs: La violencia y la intimidación impidieron que los votantes negros y sus aliados llegaran a las urnas

choices.text: The Klan was founded in Pulaski, Tennessee, in 1866
choices.textEs: El Klan se fundó en Pulaski, Tennessee, en 1866
choices.explanation: True, and it is a where rather than a why. The question asks what the founding did to Reconstruction government, and naming the town leaves that unanswered.
choices.misconception: answers where the Klan was founded rather than what its founding did

items.dokRationale: The student has to connect a form of violence to a political outcome — why intimidation at the polls removes a government's base of support. Naming the Klan as violent would be recall; explaining how that violence unseated governments is a relationship.
items.explanation: Reconstruction governments rested on Black voters and on the white Republicans who worked with them. Night-riding, whipping and murder raised the price of voting and of holding office high enough that turnout and candidacies collapsed across whole counties, which is why Congress answered with the Enforcement Acts of 1870 and 1871.
items.explanationEs: Los gobiernos de la Reconstrucción se apoyaban en los votantes negros y en los republicanos blancos que trabajaban con ellos. Las cabalgatas nocturnas, los azotes y los asesinatos elevaron tanto el precio de votar y de ocupar un cargo que la participación y las candidaturas se hundieron en condados enteros, por lo que el Congreso respondió con las Leyes de Ejecución de 1870 y 1871.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable

items.stem: After Reconstruction ended, how did lynching work in the South?
items.stemEs: Después del fin de la Reconstrucción, ¿cómo funcionaban los linchamientos en el Sur?

choices.text: As terror that enforced white control without any trial
choices.textEs: Como terror que imponía el control blanco sin ningún juicio

choices.text: Documented by the Memphis journalist Ida B. Wells in her 1892 pamphlet Southern Horrors
choices.textEs: Documentados por la periodista de Memphis Ida B. Wells en su panfleto de 1892 Southern Horrors
choices.explanation: Wells did document it, from Memphis, and her investigation is why much of the record exists at all. That answers who exposed lynching rather than how it worked.
choices.misconception: answers who documented lynching rather than how it functioned

choices.text: As a punishment imposed by Southern courts after a jury verdict
choices.textEs: Como un castigo impuesto por los tribunales del Sur tras el veredicto de un jurado
choices.explanation: Lynching was by definition outside the courts: no charge, no trial, no verdict. Reading it as a sentence misses the thing that made it terror rather than law.
choices.misconception: treats extralegal killing as a judicial punishment

choices.text: Violence aimed mainly at white Republican officeholders
choices.textEs: Violencia dirigida principalmente a los funcionarios republicanos blancos
choices.explanation: White Republicans were attacked, especially in the Klan's first years, but the great majority of those lynched after Reconstruction were Black Southerners. The choice of target is what reveals the practice's purpose.
choices.misconception: takes attacks on white Republicans as the main pattern of lynching

items.dokRationale: The student has to explain a function rather than recall a definition — why killing outside the law served political and economic control. Identifying lynching as murder would be recall.
items.explanation: Lynching after Reconstruction was public and went unpunished, and that was the point: it announced that Black Southerners who prospered, voted or refused deference could be killed with no consequence to the killers. Wells's own investigation showed that the accusations offered afterwards usually collapsed on inspection.
items.explanationEs: Los linchamientos posteriores a la Reconstrucción eran públicos y quedaban impunes, y eso era precisamente el objetivo: anunciaban que los sureños negros que prosperaban, votaban o se negaban a mostrar sumisión podían ser asesinados sin consecuencia alguna para los asesinos. La investigación de Wells demostró que las acusaciones ofrecidas después casi siempre se derrumbaban al examinarlas.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable
